title: GPU entitlement orchestration grid — forward assignment & fallback plan
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational planning sheet (grid) to assign contracted GPU slots to customers, define fallback regions, and encode quick-ops instructions for day-of allocation changes. Designed to be used by the capacity on-call and customer success during peak events.

High-level assumptions:
- All numbers are GPU-card counts (not vGPUs).
- Primary region assignment tries to respect customer geography, contract SLAs, and latency pins.
- Target utilization: 70% steady-state across committed pools, with 10% regional buffer for burst.
- Burst policy: allow up to 25% temporary burst per customer if global unallocated pool has slack; bursts auto-expire after 6 hours unless manually extended.
- Fallback hierarchy: same-region spare -> nearest-region spare -> compatible-quantized-variant in other region -> hosted overflow (best-effort).

Quick reference table (rows = customer slices):
| Contract | Customer | Region (primary) | Reserved GPUs | GPU Type | Start | End | Monthly hours committed | Priority | Allocation strategy | Fallback target | Notes |
| C-2038-A | BrightHealth Labs | us-west1 | 64 | A100-80GB | 2029-11-01 | 2032-10-31 | 30,720 | 1 (SLA) | Pinned tranche across 2 pods, even spread | us-west2 spare pool | Sensitive PII; on-prem KMS integration in rollout Q2 2030 |
| C-2041-B | KiteData | eu-west3 | 48 | H100-80GB | 2030-03-15 | 2031-03-14 | 21,600 | 2 | Soft pin by rack tag, allow cross-rack reassign | eu-central1 spot pool | Expect periodic model training spikes M/W/F 
| C-2047-C | AtlasRetail | ap-southeast1 | 32 | A100-80GB | 2030-06-01 | 2033-05-31 | 15,360 | 3 | Region-first allocation, monthly reserved windows | ap-northeast1 buffer slab | Retail peak season Oct-Nov needs extra 8 GPUs |
| C-2050-D | NimbusAI (pilot) | us-east1 | 12 | T4-16GB | 2030-01-10 | 2031-01-09 | 5,184 | 4 (pilot) | Shared micro-pool with preemptible fallback | us-east2 micro-burst | Pilot; convert to reserved if utilization > 60% for 2 months |
| C-2055-E | ZenSure | eu-north1 | 20 | H100-80GB | 2030-09-01 | 2032-08-31 | 9,600 | 2 | Multi-region mirror: primary + hot-standby | eu-west3 mirror | Compliance window: blackout for migration 2029-12 |

Derived fields & KPIs (how to read):
- "Monthly hours committed" = Reserved GPUs * 24 * days_in_month (use 30 for planning simplification).
- "Priority": 1 = SLA-backed guaranteed (auto-preempt of lower tiers), 4 = best-effort / pilot.
- Regional buffer target = ceil(sum(reserved in region) * 0.10). Keep an eye when buffer < 8 GPUs.
- Effective available pool = region_unallocated + cross-region transferable - expected_burst_reservations.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Day-of capacity shortfall detection: alert if actual utilization > 85% for > 30m in any region.
2) On-call action: open a temporary burst ticket (JIRA-INFRA-XXXX), notify CS owners for affected contracts, and apply fallback policy in order until utilization normalizes.
3) If national/regional outage: promote pre-configured mirror targets; for SLA 1 customers, shift traffic to hot-standby and mark cross-region replication event.
4) Post-mortem: annotate allocation change with tag "alloc-change:<date>" and add note to contract row.

Allocation heuristics (pseudo):
- Step A: Try to place tranche into pinned racks (respecting GPU type and quantization profile).
- Step B: If pinned racks exhausted, attempt cross-rack same-region assignment within same availability slice.
- Step C: If same-region cannot satisfy and customer priority <=2, attempt nearest-region transfer with network pinning.
- Step D: If transfer invoked, apply 10% additional buffer for mirror start-up (deduct from global spare).

Capacity planning checks to run weekly (automation suggestions):
- WeeklyJob: region_capacity_snapshot -> compute buffer_ratio and report rows where buffer_ratio < 0.12.
- WeeklyJob: contract_utilization_trend -> flag contracts with moving-average utilization > 65% over 14 days (candidate for upsell or convert to dedicated scale-up).
- MonthlyJob: reservation-entropy -> detect many small reservations causing fragmentation; propose compaction windows.

Example escalation scenarios (short cases):
- Scenario: us-west1 sudden 30% capacity loss due to rack failure.
  Actions: drain affected pods, migrate SLA-1 customers to us-west2 hot-standby, apply burst from global spare, notify sales + legal for impacted contracts.
- Scenario: simultaneous training spikes (KiteData + AtlasRetail).
  Actions: use priority-based preemption (pilot -> priority3 -> priority2), open burst requests, postpone non-critical scheduled maintenance.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Agree on global spillover cap per region vs unlimited best-effort (proposal: cap = 18 GPUs per region for hosted overflow).
- Standardize the minimal burst expiry (6h vs 12h).
- Should pilots auto-upgrade after 60% utilization for 60 days or require manual approval?

Action items (owners):
- Marco: build the automation job region_capacity_snapshot (due 2031-02-20).
- Aisha: add contract tags for encryption and compliance flags in contract metadata (due 2031-02-28).
- Sofia: coordinate the cross-region mirror test with ZenSure for March 2031 (create test ticket).

Notes to on-call: keep this sheet open during major incidents; annotate any temporary assignment with date/user and link to the incident Jira.

Revision history:
- 2029-11-05: initial draft (Sofia).
- 2030-04-12: added pilots + burst policy adjustments (Marco).
- 2031-02-12: updated table with current contracts and added automation tasks (Sofia).
